C005.subject: AGI
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: AGI within 10 years]

[PATH:empirical] Annual evaluation of scaling laws and emergent capabilities in large language models (e.g., GPT-5, Gemini Ultra) on scientific reasoning benchmarks (e.g., GPQA, MMLU-STEM) — If current scaling trends continue to yield diminishing returns on novel reasoning tasks within 3-5 years, this would refute the hypothesis that a single breakthrough is sufficient. Conversely, if emergent abilities plateau, it would support the need for a new algorithm.

[PATH:literature] Meta-analysis of progress in neurosymbolic AI and differentiable program synthesis (e.g., DeepMind's AlphaFold successor, OpenAI's process reward models) — Systematic review of recent breakthroughs in hybrid architectures could identify whether existing approaches are converging on a general reasoning architecture or remain task-specific, thus evaluating the plausibility of a single architectural leap.

[PATH:theoretical] Theoretical analysis of computational complexity and sample efficiency of current deep learning paradigms (e.g., work by Chollet, LeCun, or Bengio on abstraction and reasoning corpus (ARC) challenges) — Formal proofs or conjectures about the limits of gradient-based learning for out-of-distribution generalization would indicate whether a fundamentally new algorithm is required, directly addressing the 'architectural breakthrough' condition.

qualifier.condition: if a single architectural breakthrough (e.g., a new learning algorithm) occurs within the next 5 years

C006.subject: AGI
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: AGI within 20 years]

[PATH:empirical] Tracking progress on AI benchmarks for scientific reasoning (e.g., ARC, GPQA, Math Olympiad) over the next decade — If performance on these narrow-domain benchmarks continues to improve exponentially, it may suggest that AGI-level reasoning is approachable within 20 years; stagnation would support the hypothesis.

[PATH:literature] Meta-analysis of expert surveys on AGI timelines (e.g., AI Impacts, Müller & Bostock 2022) with focus on scientific reasoning domain — Aggregating expert forecasts can reveal consensus trends and identify key assumptions that underpin the 20-year threshold, helping to confirm or refute the hypothesis.

[PATH:theoretical] Theoretical analysis of computational and algorithmic requirements for general scientific reasoning (e.g., scaling laws, sample efficiency, causal inference) — If fundamental theoretical barriers (e.g., need for true causal understanding or abstract reasoning beyond current architectures) are identified, it would support that AGI is not achievable within 20 years; otherwise, the hypothesis weakens.

C007.subject: AGI
C007.object: only if a single monolithic architecture is abandoned in favor of a modular, neuro-symbolic system
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: AGI only if a single monolithic architecture is abandoned in favor of a modular, neuro-symbolic system]

[PATH:empirical] Comparative benchmarking of monolithic end-to-end neural architectures (e.g., GPT-4, Gemini) versus modular neuro-symbolic systems (e.g., DeepMind's ALPHA, IBM's Neuro-Symbolic AI) on tasks requiring compositional generalization, reasoning, and transfer learning (e.g., ARC, bAbI, CLEVR) — Direct empirical comparison can reveal whether modular neuro-symbolic systems outperform monolithic models on key AGI-relevant capabilities, providing evidence for or against the necessity of such an architectural shift.

[PATH:theoretical] Theoretical analysis of computational complexity and expressiveness in monolithic vs. modular architectures, drawing on results from circuit complexity, learning theory, and cognitive science (e.g., Fodor & Pylyshyn's systematicity argument, Marcus's 'deep learning is not enough' thesis) — A theoretical grounding can clarify whether monolithic architectures face fundamental limitations (e.g., in handling symbolic reasoning, compositionality, or causal inference) that modular, neuro-symbolic systems can overcome, thus supporting or refuting the hypothesis at a principled level.

[PATH:literature] Literature review of historical and contemporary AGI roadmaps and failed monolithic approaches (e.g., DARPA's AI efforts, Cyc, early neural networks) versus successful modular systems in narrow AI (e.g., AlphaFold, self-driving car stacks) — Analyzing documented successes and failures in AI history can provide inductive evidence about the necessity of modularity and neuro-symbolic integration for achieving general intelligence, helping to assess the hypothesis's plausibility.

qualifier.temporal: as of current AI research paradigms (2020s)

C008.subject: AGI
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: AGI within 20 years]

[PATH:empirical] Tracking compute scaling trends and algorithmic efficiency gains in leading AI labs (e.g., Epoch AI reports, OpenAI, DeepMind publications) — If historical trends in compute and efficiency continue to follow a power law, extrapolation may indicate whether human-level AGI requires resources beyond what is plausible within 20 years. Deviations or saturation would refute the hypothesis.

[PATH:literature] Meta-analysis of cognitive architecture benchmarks and limitations of current large models (e.g., ARC-AGI, BIG-bench, and adversarial testing for generalization and causal reasoning) — Systematic review of empirical failures in out-of-distribution generalization, long-term planning, and common sense could show fundamental barriers that make AGI unlikely within the timeframe, or reveal unexpected progress.

[PATH:theoretical] Theoretical analysis of computational complexity of general intelligence (e.g., Hutter's AIXI framework, Chollet's 'measure of intelligence') — Formal proofs or complexity bounds on the minimal computational resources required for human-level AGI could provide upper or lower bounds on feasibility, helping confirm or refute the 20-year timeline.

C011.subject: AGI
C011.predicate: will not be achieved within 20 years
C011.object: if binding global safety regulations are enacted within 5 years
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: AGI if binding global safety regulations are enacted within 5 years]

[PATH:empirical] Historical analysis of regulatory impact on high-risk technology development timelines (e.g., nuclear weapons, synthetic biology, or AI) — Examining past cases where binding global regulations were enacted early in a technology's lifecycle can reveal whether such regulations significantly delayed or redirected development milestones, providing an analog for AGI.

[PATH:empirical] Expert elicitation surveys on AGI timelines under different regulatory scenarios (e.g., from AI Impacts, Epoch AI, or similar forecasting efforts) — Comparing expert forecasts with and without binding safety regulations can directly test whether such regulations are expected to push AGI beyond a 20-year horizon, offering quantitative evidence for the hypothesis.

[PATH:theoretical] Formal models of AI research investment and progression under regulatory constraints (e.g., using economic or game-theoretic frameworks) — Building and analyzing models that incorporate regulatory compliance costs, reduced funding, and shifted research incentives can predict whether binding regulations could plausibly delay AGI by 20 years, helping to confirm or refute the causal claim.

scope.domain: impact of regulatory frameworks on AGI timelines

C012.subject: AGI
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: AGI within 20 years]

[PATH:literature] Historical accuracy of prior AI timeline predictions (e.g., from AI Impacts or Meta-analysis of expert surveys on AGI timelines) — Systematic review of past expert forecasts and historical prediction accuracy can calibrate confidence in current 20-year AGI claims, testing whether such predictions tend to be overconfident or accurate.

[PATH:empirical] Tracking empirical scaling laws and compute trends (e.g., from Epoch AI or semi-annual reports on frontier model capabilities and required compute) — If scaling laws for performance continue without plateau and compute growth outpaces algorithmic efficiency gains, it may support feasibility within 20 years; if diminishing returns or physical limits appear, it would refute the hypothesis.

[PATH:theoretical] Theoretical analysis of necessary cognitive architectures and unsolved AI-hard problems (e.g., from the AGI Safety Fundamentals curriculum or papers on the 'bitter lesson' vs. 'symbolic gaps') — Examining whether current deep learning paradigms can bridge key gaps (e.g., long-term reasoning, causal inference, common sense) provides a theoretical basis for whether AGI is achievable within a fixed time horizon.
